proposed_statement_changes.proposed: Specialize \(\texttt{def:lipschitz-lower-pair}\) to \(\alpha=1\) and \(\kappa=2\). For every \(0<h\leq1/4\), both members of \(P_h^{\mathrm{pair}}=(P_{0,h},P_{1,h})\) belong to \(\mathcal P_{1,1,1,2,L}\), and \[|\theta(P_{1,h})-\theta(P_{0,h})|=h^2/8,\qquad \operatorname{TV}(P_{0,h},P_{1,h})=h^4/96,\qquad \operatorname{KL}(P_{0,h},P_{1,h})\leq h^5/240.\] For \(n\geq4^5\), \(h=n^{-1/5}\) gives the clean two-point lower rate \(n^{-2/5}\), while \(h=1/4\) covers the remaining finite set of sample sizes after adjusting the constant. For \(0<\epsilon\leq1/10\), with \(h=\{\epsilon/(1-\epsilon)\}^{1/4}/4\), the explicit contaminants satisfy \(R_h=(1-\epsilon)P_{0,h}+\epsilon Q_{0,h}=(1-\epsilon)P_{1,h}+\epsilon Q_{1,h}\), and the clean targets are separated by a constant multiple of \(\{\epsilon/(1-\epsilon)\}^{1/2}\).
proposed_statement_changes.reason: At \(\epsilon=0\), the displayed scale is \(h=0\), outside the domain \(0<h\leq1/4\), and \(Q_{0,h},Q_{1,h}\) are defined by \(\texttt{def:lipschitz-lower-pair}\) only when \(\epsilon>0\). Restricting only the explicit-collision sentence to \(0<\epsilon\leq1/10\) makes the claim well typed; the zero-contamination risk assertion remains supplied by the generalized lemma.
